note: Audited the tree on 2026-08-07 against sprint-plan.md's claim that every sprint has shipped. It has not: Sprint 3's real-time issue stream was never built. hooks/useIssues.ts has no socket and no poll; server.ts emits for chat, typing and console-logs but nothing for issues; io is not even exported, so there is no seam to emit from. The other four Sprint 3 items did ship, which is the likely reason the row was marked done. Sprint 7's ledger archived under .agents/docs/archive/sprint-7-hardening-*.

features.title: lib/realtime.ts registry — a seam to emit from
features.description: R-D4. `io` is constructed in server.ts and never exported, so api/ingest.ts has nothing to call. Importing server.ts from a route is a cycle. A tiny set-at-boot registry is the seam.
steps: server.ts registers the io instance at boot
api/ingest.ts imports only the registry, never server.ts
A call before boot is a no-op, not a crash
FAILURE CASE: no import cycle — verified by the build, not by reading
features.notes: 2026-08-20. server/src/lib/realtime.ts + realtime.test.ts (4 assertions). server.ts:60 registers io at boot. Before-boot emit returns false and does not throw; a throwing transport is swallowed and reported false. No-cycle proof is stronger than a read: the module's only import is `import type`, so dist/lib/realtime.js emits zero require() calls — there is no runtime edge to form a cycle through. The 'ingest imports only the registry' half of step 2 is asserted under F003, where that import is actually written.

features.title: project:<id> room, gated by resolveMembership
features.description: R-D3. Joining is authorized, not merely authenticated. An authenticated-only room is a cross-project leak — the third occurrence of the defect that deleted the :8082 relay and forced the monitors room to gate itself.
steps: A member joining project:<id> succeeds
A signed-in NON-member joining is refused
The SDK's anonymous socket cannot join
FAILURE CASE: a non-member receives ZERO frames for that project, asserted on the wire, not by an empty UI
features.notes: 2026-08-20. lib/issueStream.ts (decision, 7 assertions) + lib/issueStreamHandler.ts driven by a REAL socket.io server and real clients in issueStreamHandler.test.ts (5 assertions). The failure case is a wire assertion as the step demands: a signed-in non-member is refused, then 5 frames are emitted into project:1 and the outsider's received array is [] after a 300ms window. Same for the anonymous SDK socket. Refusal string is identical for 'no such project' and 'not yours' so the socket is not a slug oracle. Membership lookup throwing fails CLOSED. Mutation-checked: admitting a null membership turns 4 of these red (named), and reverting turns them green.

features.title: Ingest emits absolute-valued deltas, post-commit and detached
features.description: R-D1 + R-D4. count is the new total, never +1: sockets drop and replay, and an increment over an unreliable transport is how a counting tool starts lying. The emit runs after the transaction commits, wrapped, and can never fail or slow ingest.
steps: An ingested error produces one frame on project:<id> within 2s
The frame carries absolute count, lastSeen, status and an isNew flag
The emit happens after commit, never inside the transaction
FAILURE CASE: with the emit forced to throw, ingest still answers 202, still writes event and issue, and is not measurably slower
features.notes: 2026-08-20. OBSERVED LIVE against the dev database, server on PORT=3010/WS=8091, a real member socket joined to project:1. Two POSTs of the same error produced exactly two frames, one each, at +858ms (cold Prisma) and +34ms — inside the 2s criterion. Frames carried absolute count 1 then 2, isNew true then false, level, status and ISO lastSeen; no issue body. FAILURE CASE observed, not argued: with emitToRoom patched to throw unconditionally and the server restarted on 3011/8092, ingest still answered 202 (149ms vs 108ms — noise, and the push runs after res.json so it cannot delay the response), the Issue row still incremented to count 2 and the Event row was still written; the throw surfaced only as 'issue activity emit failed' in the server log. The emit loop got its own try/catch: the outer catch would otherwise answer 500 after the 202 was already sent. The frame for a regression is built from the reopened row, so it arrives as unresolved rather than resolved. Unit side: buildIssueFrame, 5 assertions including an idempotence check that applying one frame twice lands on the same count.

features.title: useIssues patches in place — no reorder, no refetch
features.description: R-D2. A push for an issue already on screen updates count, lastSeen and status in place. Re-sorting a list under a reading cursor is the thing that makes people close the tab.
steps: The count on a visible issue increments in place
The list does not reorder and does not refetch
Two windows on the same project both update, within 2s, once each

features.title: New issues: conditional prepend, banner when filtered
features.description: R-D2. The server room does not know the client's filter, so insertion has to be decided where the query state lives. Injecting a row that does not match the active filter makes the filter look broken.
steps: isNew on page 1 with no filters prepends and the list still holds exactly pageSize rows
isNew with a filter active does NOT insert; an 'N new issues' banner appears
isNew on page > 1 does NOT insert
Clicking the banner refetches the current query
FAILURE CASE: a push for a project the client is not viewing is ignored

features.title: No double-applied optimistic updates
features.description: The named risk in the plan and the top item in the pre-mortem. A local optimistic update and the echoed server push both land on the same row; absolute values are what make that harmless.
steps: Resolve an issue in window A; window B shows resolved once
Window A shows no flicker and no doubled count
Promoting an issue to a ticket behaves the same way

features.title: Three-state connection badge, never 'live' over a dead feed
features.description: R-D5. 'Nothing is happening' and 'the page stopped listening' look identical, and that is the worst failure a monitoring view has. A boolean cannot express the difference.
steps: Kill the server: the badge goes reconnecting, then offline
It never reads live while the feed is dead
Restart: it reconnects, refetches the current query, and the list is correct
FAILURE CASE: pushes missed while disconnected are recovered by the refetch, not lost

features.title: Socket handshake refreshes its token once
features.description: R-D6, and the one that decides whether this sprint is real. lib/authSession.ts covers four HTTP transports and explicitly not sockets. A tab past token expiry reconnects with a stale token, io.use throws, and the feed dies silently while the page still renders signed-in — the exact shape of the Sprint 1 defect.
steps: Leave a tab open past access-token expiry: it keeps streaming
The refresh goes through the existing single-flight coordinator, not a second implementation
A second consecutive auth failure signs out rather than looping
FAILURE CASE: the anonymous-socket path stays open for the SDK — do not tighten io.use as a side effect

features.title: The suite proves its worth: reintroduce the count drift
features.description: Same discipline as Sprint 7's F011. A test that has never failed has proven nothing, and count drift is the failure this whole design is shaped to prevent.
steps: Reintroduce an increment-based count (count += 1) and the suite goes red naming the drift
Reintroduce a blind insert under an active filter and the suite goes red
Both revert clean and the suite goes green

features.title: Clean build, green suite, and the plan corrected
features.description: sprint-plan.md:375 claims every sprint has shipped. It is the document-precedence rule's own failure mode, and it gets fixed in the same PR as the code rather than 'at the end'.
steps: tsc --noEmit, eslint src and npm run build clean in both workspaces
npm test green in CI from a clean checkout
sprint-plan.md's 'every sprint has now shipped' line corrected with what was actually missing
realtime-issue-stream.md gains its exit notes
